name: Anakeesta
description: Mountaintop theme park accessed by chondola. Treewalk village, ziplines, Cliff Top bar, gem mining, and killer views. Feels more 'mountain experience' than theme park.
must_try: Treetop Skywalk and the Cliff Top Bar sunset

name: Dollywood Theme Park
address: 2700 Dollywood Parks Blvd, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: 160 acres, 50+ rides, world-class entertainment, award-winning food. Lightning Rod is the world's fastest wooden coaster. NightFlight Expedition (Spring 2026) is a $50M hybrid coaster/river ride — first of its kind. 11 USA Today 10Best nominations in 2026.
must_try: NightFlight Expedition (new 2026), Lightning Rod, Wildwood Grove, and the cinnamon bread
hours: Seasonal — generally late March through early January
seasonal: Open seasonally. Four major festivals: I Will Always Love You (spring), Summer Celebration, Harvest Festival (fall), Smoky Mountain Christmas (winter).

name: Dollywood's Splash Country
address: 2700 Dollywood Parks Blvd, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: 35-acre water park adjacent to Dollywood. Tennessee's first water coaster, wave pool, lazy river. New Neon Nights after-hours event in 2026.
must_try: Firetower Falls and TailSpin Racer

name: Ober Mountain Ski Area & Amusement Park
description: Ski area (small but it exists), aerial tramway, ice skating, alpine slide, wildlife encounter. Accessed from downtown Gatlinburg via the aerial tram.
must_try: Aerial tramway and the alpine coaster
seasonal: Skiing Dec-Mar; rest of attractions year-round

name: Speedwerkz Exotic Car Experience
description: Drive or ride in exotic supercars on a controlled course. Lamborghinis, Ferraris, McLarens. Next door to Ole Red. Absolute blast for car people.
must_try: The Lamborghini experience

name: The Island in Pigeon Forge
address: 131 The Island Dr, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: Open-air entertainment complex with The Great Smoky Mountain Wheel (200 ft), rides, shops, restaurants, and a fountain show. Free to walk around. Guy Fieri's Flavortown is here.
must_try: The Great Smoky Mountain Wheel at sunset and the fountain show

name: Gatlinburg SkyLift Park
description: Chairlift to the top of Crockett Mountain. The SkyBridge — North America's longest pedestrian suspension bridge — is the draw. Glass floor panels. Terrifying and beautiful.
must_try: Walk across the SkyBridge glass panels

name: Ripley's Aquarium of the Smokies
description: One of the best aquariums in the Southeast. Shark tunnel with moving walkway, penguin encounters, touch tanks. Perfect rainy day backup.
must_try: Shark Lagoon tunnel and the penguin playhouse

name: Titanic Museum Attraction
description: Half-scale Titanic replica housing 400+ artifacts. You get a boarding pass with a real passenger's name. Interactive galleries. Way better than it sounds.
must_try: Touch the iceberg replica and check your passenger's fate

name: Bijou Theatre
description: Intimate 700-seat venue in a historic 1909 building. Live music from indie to bluegrass. Knoxville's best small-venue concert experience.
must_try: Check the live music calendar

name: Dolly Parton's Stampede
description: Dinner show with horses, stunts, music, and a four-course feast you eat with your hands. Wildly over-the-top in the best possible way. Kids lose their minds.
must_try: The whole experience — it's a package deal

name: Great Smoky Mountain Murder Mystery Dinner Show
description: Intimate, side-splitting comedy whodunit relying heavily on audience participation. Fantastic alternative to the massive arena dinner shows.
must_try: The Moonshine Murders show

name: Hatfield & McCoy Dinner Feud
description: High-energy, over-the-top hillbilly feud featuring diving dogs, stunts, and all-you-can-eat Southern comfort food. Pure Pigeon Forge spectacle.
must_try: The creamy soup served with dinner

name: Pirates Voyage Dinner & Show
description: Pirate-themed dinner show with a massive indoor lagoon, acrobatics, and a pirate ship battle. Another Dolly Parton production.
must_try: Indoor lagoon pirate battle

name: Tennessee Theatre
description: 1928 movie palace turned performance venue. The 'Jewel of the South.' Wurlitzer organ still plays before shows. Live music, comedy, film. Gorgeous interior.
must_try: Any show — the architecture alone is worth the ticket

name: Gatlinburg Brewing Company
description: Craft beer, pizza, and live music/comedy. More polished than the typical Parkway spot. Good rotating tap list.
must_try: Craft pizza and whatever's rotating on tap

name: Smoky Mountain Brewery - Gatlinburg
description: Original brewery in Gatlinburg with a deck overlooking the Smokies. Cherokee Red Ale and Mountain Light are the house staples. Live music Mon-Sat. Great sports bar energy.
must_try: Beer sampler flight with Cherokee Red Ale

name: Tennessee Stud Cider
description: Hard cider tastings right on the Parkway. Apple pie, blueberry, pineapple flavors. Good stop if you're not a beer or moonshine person.
must_try: Apple Pie hard cider

name: Cliff Top Bar & Grill at Anakeesta
description: Requires Anakeesta ticket to access. Take the chondola to the top of the mountain. The views make it worth the admission price alone.
must_try: Cocktails with the 360-degree mountain view

name: Maple Hall
description: Upscale bowling alley + cocktail bar + restaurant on Gay Street. Boutique bowling lanes, craft drinks, live music. Sounds gimmicky but it's genuinely cool.
must_try: Bowl a few frames with a craft cocktail

name: Peter Kern Library
description: Speakeasy inside The Oliver Hotel. Look for the red light in the alley. Craft cocktails, intimate setting, literary theme. One of the best bars in Tennessee.
must_try: Old Fashioned or the seasonal cocktail menu

name: The Casual Pint
description: Huge craft beer selection in a chill taproom. Good place to try Tennessee craft beers without the noise of the bigger bars.
must_try: Flight of Tennessee craft beers

name: Doc Collier Moonshine Distillery
description: Family recipe moonshine with English Mountain Spring Water. The Firecracker cinnamon shine and the 'shined cherries from Traverse City are the standouts.
must_try: Firecracker cinnamon moonshine

name: Junction 35 Spirits
description: At The Mountain Mile in Pigeon Forge. Moonshine, gin, rum, bourbon — broader portfolio than most. Watermelon and Sour Gummy Worm moonshine for the adventurous.
must_try: Sour Gummy Worm moonshine

name: King's Family Distillery
description: Husband-and-wife operation just outside Pigeon Forge. Most awarded bourbon in the Smoky Mountains. Premium small-batch feel.
must_try: Award-winning bourbon

name: Old Forge Distillery
address: 170 Old Mill Ave, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: At the historic Old Mill. Uses grains from the actual grist mill. Small-batch with vapor infusion. 1830 Original Moonshine is the signature.
must_try: 1830 Original Moonshine

name: Ole Smoky Moonshine Distillery - The Holler
description: Most visited distillery in America. Free live music, working stills you can watch, $5 tastings of 20+ moonshine flavors. Apple Pie and White Lightnin' are the classics. Dogs welcome.
must_try: Apple Pie moonshine and the free live music stage

name: Sugarlands Distilling Co.
description: Higher-end moonshine operation. $5 tasting of 12+ flavors. The back bar is the real gem — cocktails in a chill patio away from the Parkway chaos. Blueberry Muffin and Maple Bacon shine.
must_try: Back bar cocktails and the Blueberry Muffin moonshine

name: Tennessee Shine Co.
address: Multiple locations: Gatlinburg, Pigeon Forge, Sevierville
description: Family-owned operation with the wildest flavors — Blue Houdini, Choco Moo Shine, Dream Cream. Three locations across the strip.
must_try: Blue Houdini and Choco Moo Shine

name: Puckers Sports Grill
description: All-you-can-eat wings on Mondays, drink specials through the week. Casual Parkway sports bar where you can actually catch a game.
must_try: Monday wing deal

name: Tom and Earl's Back Alley Grill
description: The locals' escape from Parkway tourist madness. Would be a great neighborhood bar anywhere — here it's an absolute treasure. Cocktails, craft beer, solid food.
must_try: Ask the bartender — they know their stuff

name: Preservation Pub
description: Three floors, rooftop bar, live music almost every night. The heartbeat of Knoxville nightlife on Market Square.
must_try: Rooftop drinks and whatever band is playing

name: Bootleggers Homemade Wine
description: Two sisters making wine by hand in small batches. Free tastings. Muscadine blush and Scuppernong (a Southern staple) are the signatures. Can't always ship — buy in person.
must_try: Homegrown Muscadine Blush

name: Sugarland Cellars
description: Winery at the entrance to GSMNP. On the local wine trail. Hellbender is the winemaster's signature. Good patio, relaxed pace.
must_try: Hellbender wine

name: The Donut Friar
description: A Gatlinburg institution since 1969. Handmade donuts, cinnamon bread, and bear claws. The line moves fast. Cash is king.
must_try: Cinnamon bread loaf

name: Coffee & Chocolate
description: Extraordinary chocolate truffles and seasonal macarons. Right next to the famous Downtown Knoxville mural.
must_try: Chocolate truffles and seasonal macarons

name: Mahalo Coffee Roasters
description: Surf-inspired specialty coffee roaster in Knoxville turning out some of the highest quality espresso in East Tennessee.
must_try: Iced Vanilla Latte

name: Towns End Coffee Co.
address: 7249 E Lamar Alexander Pkwy, Townsend, TN 37882
description: Excellent artisanal coffee shop on the peaceful side of the Smokies. Perfect pit stop before heading into Cades Cove.
must_try: Locally roasted drip coffee and breakfast burritos

name: Kilwins Gatlinburg
description: Premium sweets shop on the Parkway with Mackinac Island fudge and high-end chocolates made in front of you.
must_try: Mackinac Island Fudge

name: Ole Smoky Candy Kitchen
description: Gatlinburg institution since 1952. Watch them stretch taffy on vintage machines in the window, then buy a freshly packed box.
must_try: Traditional Taffylogs

name: The Fudgery at The Island
address: 131 Island Dr Suite 3106-B, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: Hand-paddled fudge with singing employees. Part treat shop, part show.
must_try: Rocky Road Fudge

name: Cruze Farm Ice Cream
description: Locally sourced, ridiculously creamy soft-serve from their own dairy farm. The retro vibe is perfect for photos.
must_try: Sweet Cream and Honey Lavender swirl

name: Kaizen
description: Incredibly popular Japanese Izakaya pub in Knoxville's Old City. Small plates, creative Asian-fusion buns, and a packed house every weekend.
must_try: Dry Spiced Pork Noodles and Steamed Buns

name: Lee's Fusion Cafe
description: Reliable Pan-Asian and Chinese takeout when you just want to eat in your cabin. The Malaysian fried rice is a local favorite.
must_try: Orange Chicken and Malaysian Roti

name: Thai Basil
description: Family-owned staple near the interstate exit with scratch-made curries. When they say 'Thai Hot,' they absolutely mean it.
must_try: Pad Thai with Tofu

name: Thai Palace
description: Unpretentious strip-mall gem beloved by locals for highly customizable spice levels and massive portions. Excellent for a quiet meal away from Parkway chaos.
must_try: Drunken Noodles

name: The Baht
description: Authentic Thai cuisine in a modernized riverfront setting right on the Gatlinburg Parkway. A welcome alternative to the heavy Southern fare dominating the strip.
must_try: Pad Kra Pao (Thai basil stir fry)

name: Calhoun's Gatlinburg
description: Mountain lodge BBQ spot. Ribs and pulled pork are what they're known for. Good for families and groups — casual enough for post-hike food.
must_try: Hickory-smoked baby back ribs

name: Dead End BBQ
description: Neighborhood Knoxville staple turning out competition-quality barbecue and inventive sides. Brisket burnt ends are phenomenal.
must_try: Mac Attack with Brisket

name: Sweet P's BBQ and Soul House
description: Top-tier Tennessee barbecue with fantastic dry rubs and incredible soul food sides. The mac and cheese is genuinely legendary.
must_try: Smoked Andouille Sausage and Pimento Cheese Dip

name: OliBea
description: The best breakfast in Knoxville's Old City. Locally sourced ingredients elevating classic Southern morning staples to an art form.
must_try: Smash Potatoes and Chicken Biscuit

name: Pancake Pantry
description: The OG pancake house. Open since 1960 — first pancake specialty restaurant in Tennessee. The line is part of the experience. Don't overthink it, just go.
must_try: Austrian apple-walnut pancakes

name: The Old Mill Restaurant
address: 164 Old Mill Ave, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: Historic 1830 water-powered grist mill with a restaurant attached. Southern comfort food with corn ground on-site. Corn chowder and fried chicken are legendary.
must_try: Corn chowder and the fried chicken

name: Split Rail Eats
description: Southern-style lunch and Sunday brunch. Uses Mahalo Coffee from Knoxville and Springer Mountain Farms chicken. The cheesesteak and brunch biscuits are the move.
must_try: Cheesesteak on ciabatta or the brunch biscuits

name: Tupelo Honey
description: Southern scratch kitchen right on Market Square. Brunch is the move — fried green tomatoes, shrimp and grits, and biscuits that hit different.
must_try: Fried green tomatoes and shrimp and grits

name: Blue Moose Burgers & Wings
description: Local chain that does burgers and wings better than they need to. The moose burger is the signature. Solid craft beer selection.
must_try: The Moose Burger and the zesty wings

name: Cafe 4
description: Market Square staple. Lobster mac and cheese, truffle fries, pimento cheese dip. The patio is the best outdoor seating downtown.
must_try: Lobster mac and cheese and the punchbowl cocktails

name: Guy Fieri's Downtown Flavortown
address: 131 The Island Dr, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: 43,000 sq ft of Guy Fieri energy at The Island. Part restaurant, part arcade, part bowling. Over-the-top in every way, which is the point.
must_try: Trash Can Nachos

name: Local Goat
description: Wildly popular scratch kitchen specializing in locally sourced, modern American pub food. Parking is tough but the burgers are worth the wait.
must_try: Deep-fried Deviled Eggs and the Elvis Burger

name: Marble City Kitchen
description: Southern comfort in the Hilton downtown. The Firefly bar next door has the only hand-selected George Dickel reserve barrel in Tennessee.
must_try: Southern plates and Firefly's reserve George Dickel bourbon

name: Mel's Classic Diner
description: 1950s diner straight out of a movie. Neon lights, jukebox, checkered floors. Burgers and milkshakes are the play. Kids love it.
must_try: Classic cheeseburger and a milkshake

name: Myrtle's Chicken + Beer
description: Fried chicken and Southern comfort food on Market Square. No-nonsense. Cold beer, hot chicken.
must_try: Fried chicken and the mac and cheese

name: Southern Comfort - Westgate Resort
description: Cajun and Creole meets Southern home cooking. Shrimp and grits, chicken and dumplings, and a mountain view. Open to non-resort guests.
must_try: Shrimp and grits

name: Tennessee Jed's
description: Newer spot on the Parkway doing creative food that actually stands out from the pancake-and-steak monotony. Small space, big flavors.
must_try: Check the rotating specials

name: Yassin's Falafel House
description: Beloved Knoxville institution serving incredibly fresh Mediterranean food with a welcoming message of community. Named 'Nicest Place in America' by Reader's Digest.
must_try: Spicy Hummus and Falafel Pita

name: Cherokee Grill and Steakhouse
description: Mountain lodge atmosphere with Cherokee artifacts on the walls. Steaks, seafood, and rotisserie chicken done right. Across from the old Ober Gatlinburg entrance.
must_try: Slow-roasted prime rib

name: Crystelle Creek Restaurant & Grill
description: Oak wood-fired steaks overlooking a creek. Nashville Prime Rib, blackened catfish, and a koi pond out back. Feels upscale without the attitude.
must_try: Nashville Prime Rib

name: Ember & Elm at HeartSong Lodge
description: Dollywood's HeartSong Lodge signature restaurant. Locally-sourced Appalachian cuisine done at a resort level. Open to non-guests.
must_try: Seasonal tasting menu

name: Gaucho Urbano Brazilian Steakhouse
description: Elegant all-you-can-eat Brazilian steakhouse bringing high-end tableside carved meats to Pigeon Forge. Perfect for celebrations.
must_try: The Chef's Harvest Table and Picanha

name: J.C. Holdway
description: James Beard Award-winning Chef Joseph Lenn's flagship. The best restaurant in the Knoxville metro, full stop. Southern ingredients with technical precision.
must_try: Chef's tasting menu or the wood-fired dishes

name: Oliver Royale
description: Inside The Oliver Hotel. Candlelit, ever-changing menu, creative cocktails. One of the most memorable dining experiences in Knoxville.
must_try: Seasonal prix fixe

name: Park Grill
description: Right at the national park entrance. Hickory-grilled steaks, rainbow trout, and a vibe that says 'mountain lodge, not chain restaurant.' Solid wine list.
must_try: Hickory-grilled rainbow trout

name: The Greenbrier Restaurant
description: Tucked off the main drag in a converted mountain home. The seared duck breast is legendary. One of the few places in town that feels like a real restaurant, not a tourist trap.
must_try: Seared duck breast

name: The Melting Pot - Gatlinburg
description: Fondue date night in the mountains. Four-course experience — cheese, salad, entree, chocolate. Not for people in a hurry.
must_try: The Big Night Out four-course experience

name: The Peddler Steakhouse
description: The best steak in Gatlinburg, full stop. They cut your meat tableside from a rolling cart. Salad bar is surprisingly good. Sits right on the river.
must_try: Custom-cut filet mignon with the French onion soup

name: Abridged Beer Company
description: Set in a 1950s auto garage, this brewpub serves some of the best pub fare and craft beer in Knoxville. Extremely family and dog-friendly.
must_try: Abridged Burger and any seasonal sour beer

name: Balter Beerworks
description: Scratch kitchen brewpub downtown. House-brewed beers and elevated bar food. The pretzel with beer cheese is essential.
must_try: Bavarian pretzel with beer cheese and a house IPA

name: Stock & Barrel
description: Burger-and-bourbon spot on Market Square. The Billy (goat cheese, bourbon onions, tomato jam) is the order. Great patio seating.
must_try: The Billy burger with bourbon onions

name: Emilia
description: Homemade Italian on Market Square. Gnocchi, focaccia, butterscotch budino. Date-night caliber with a warm, modern vibe.
must_try: Handmade gnocchi and the butterscotch budino

name: Loco Burro Fresh Mex Cantina
description: Rooftop bar with Parkway people-watching, massive margaritas, and a mechanical donkey inside. It's the fun-tourist stop that locals actually also like.
must_try: Giant margarita on the rooftop

name: Big Daddy's Pizzeria
description: Wood-fired brick oven pizza with incredibly fresh ingredients. They don't own a freezer — hand-pulled dough is the standard here.
must_try: The Taco Pie or Big Kahuna

name: Nino's Pizzeria & Eatery
description: True hidden local gem off the main drag with massive NY-style slices and authentic Italian entrees. Locals try to keep this one quiet.
must_try: Pepperoni Knots and Cannolis

name: Pizza Rio - Gatlinburg
description: Perched above the river, same endless Brazilian pizza experience right on the Gatlinburg strip. Upscale feel for a pizza joint.
must_try: Picanha Pizza

name: Pizza Rio - Pigeon Forge
description: Brazilian rodizio-style pizzeria where servers continuously bring fresh slices to your table. All-you-can-eat marathon of savory and sweet pies.
must_try: The continuous dessert pizza service

name: Chesapeake's Restaurant - Gatlinburg
description: Fancy seafood in a mountain town sounds wrong but this place makes it work. Raw bar, blue-lit interiors, views of the river. Gatlinburg's best-kept upscale secret.
must_try: Fresh Maine lobster and the raw bar

name: Crawdaddy's Restaurant & Oyster Bar
description: Lively Cajun-style joint on the Parkway with a great balcony for people-watching. A loud slice of New Orleans in the mountains.
must_try: Lobster & Shrimp Dip and Alligator Bites

name: Harpoon Harry's Crab House
address: 112 Walden's Main St, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: Massive wood-timber restaurant blending coastal seafood with mountain aesthetics. Excellent fresh catches and a huge bar area.
must_try: Spinach Crab & Artichoke Dip

name: Huck Finn's Catfish
description: All-you-can-eat catfish that's genuinely great. Old-school Southern joint — no frills, just perfect fried fish. Huge portions, cheap prices.
must_try: All-you-can-eat catfish dinner

name: STIR Knoxville
description: Old City open-air concept with a heated patio. Craft cocktails over a dozen oysters. The date night spot for the Knoxville crowd.
must_try: Oysters and a craft cocktail on the patio

name: The Brass Pearl
description: Raw oyster bar on Market Square. Fresh seafood, coastal vibes in a mountain city. Same owners as Stock & Barrel — they know what they're doing.
must_try: Dozen oysters and the fish tacos

name: MagiQuest
description: Massive castle-themed complex with live-action role-playing using magic wands, plus blacklight pirate golf and a mirror maze.
must_try: The interactive wand quests

name: Ripley's Believe It or Not! Odditorium
description: The classic Odditorium — three stories of bizarre artifacts, interactive exhibits, and pop-culture oddities.
must_try: The shrunken heads exhibit

name: Ripley's Haunted Adventure
description: Year-round multi-million dollar haunted house with live actors and animatronics. Genuinely spooky — great for thrill-seeking teens.
must_try: The creepy elevator ride to start

name: Ripley's Mirror Maze
description: Disorienting LED-lit labyrinth of mirrors that's surprisingly tricky to navigate. Quick, fun Parkway stop.
must_try: Navigating without using your hands

name: TopJump Trampoline & Extreme Arena
description: Indoor trampoline park and ninja course — absolute lifesaver on a rainy day when the kids need to burn off energy.
must_try: Fire & Ice Ninja Course

name: Illusionation: The Magic of Jason Hudy
description: High-energy blend of world-class illusions and comedy. Slick, well-produced show right on the main strip.
must_try: Volunteer for an on-stage illusion

name: Steven Best's Smoky Mountain Theater
address: 157 E Wears Valley Rd #12, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: Intimate, up-close magic and illusion show leaning heavily on audience participation. Great evening entertainment without the arena crowds.
must_try: Unbelievable Magic Show

name: Gatlin's Escape Games
description: Top-tier escape rooms with fantastic local themes right in downtown Gatlinburg. Challenging but perfectly logical puzzles.
must_try: Moonshine Hill Hootenanny

name: The Escape Game - Pigeon Forge
address: 131 The Island Dr Suite 9139, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: High-budget, incredibly immersive escape rooms at The Island. Production quality rivals major theme parks.
must_try: The Prison Break room

name: The Track - Pigeon Forge
description: Classic all-in-one family fun center with multi-level wooden go-kart tracks, bumper boats, and a massive arcade.
must_try: The Wild Woody elevated go-kart track

name: Xtreme Racing Center
description: Fastest professional-grade European Sodi karts in Pigeon Forge. Elevated and linear tracks provide serious adrenaline.
must_try: The 3,500 linear foot Xtreme Track

name: Crave Golf Club
description: Wildly colorful candy-themed indoor and outdoor mini-golf complex. It literally smells like sugar when you walk in.
must_try: The indoor rooftop course

name: Hillbilly Golf
description: Legendary Gatlinburg classic — ride an incline tram up the mountain to play 18 holes winding down a steep, heavily wooded hillside.
must_try: The tram ride to the top

name: The Oliver Hotel
description: Boutique hotel in a restored 1876 building. Home to Peter Kern Library speakeasy and Oliver Royale restaurant. Steps from Market Square. Knoxville's best hotel.
must_try: Stay here and hit Peter Kern Library downstairs

name: Auntie Belham's Cabin Rentals
description: Long-standing, reliable cabin rental agency across the entire county. They provide excellent free attraction ticket packages at check-in.
must_try: The free attraction tickets provided at check-in

name: Cabins for YOU
description: One of the largest property management companies in the Smokies. Everything from secluded romantic hideaways to massive corporate luxury lodges.
must_try: Their pet-friendly secluded cabin options

name: Elk Springs Resort
description: Luxury cabin resort on 68 private acres bordering the National Park. Cabins feature high-end amenities including private indoor pools.
must_try: Booking a cabin with an indoor heated pool

name: Gatlinburg Falls Resort
description: Sprawling resort community minutes from downtown Gatlinburg with massive multi-level cabins designed for large groups and family reunions.
must_try: Cabins with arcade rooms and home theaters

name: Elkmont Campground
description: Most popular campground in GSMNP. Along the Little River. Firefly viewing in June. Reserve way ahead. Where the synchronous firefly lottery happens.
must_try: June synchronous firefly event (lottery required)

name: Smokemont Campground
description: Beautiful, serene National Park campground with tent and RV sites right on the Oconaluftee River. Great basecamp for the North Carolina side of the Smokies.
must_try: Wildlife viewing near the Oconaluftee River

name: Black Fox Lodge - Tapestry Collection by Hilton
description: Modern upscale lodge vibes right on the river in the middle of Pigeon Forge. Outdoor pool and waterslide.
must_try: The outdoor pool and waterslide

name: Edgewater Hotel & Conference Center
description: Convenient hotel right on the river, steps from the Aquarium and downtown Gatlinburg shops. Indoor/outdoor pool and complimentary breakfast.
must_try: Indoor/outdoor pool and complimentary breakfast

name: Margaritaville Island Hotel
address: 131 The Island Dr, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: Island attitude meets mountain latitude. Rooftop pool and Chill Bar at The Island complex. Walking distance to everything on the strip. Jimmy Buffett energy.
must_try: Rooftop pool and margaritas at the Chill Bar

name: The Inn at Christmas Place
address: 119 Christmas Tree Lane, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: Bavarian-style hotel where it's Christmas 365 days a year. The attention to detail and holiday cheer is completely unmatched. Peak occupancy year-round.
must_try: The Santa Suite and the Glockenspiel performances

name: The Park Vista - DoubleTree by Hilton
description: Iconic circular high-rise perched on a mountain above Gatlinburg. Stunning panoramic views from private balconies. Trolley runs from the lobby to downtown.
must_try: Riding the trolley from the lobby into downtown

name: Dollywood's DreamMore Resort and Spa
description: Dollywood's flagship resort. Priority park access, complimentary TimeSaver passes, shuttle to parks. Spa, pool, Song & Hearth restaurant. Mountain luxury without pretension.
must_try: Stay-and-play package for complimentary TimeSaver passes

name: Dollywood's HeartSong Lodge & Resort
description: Newest Dollywood resort (opened 2023). Nature-inspired design, Ember & Elm restaurant, pool, spa. Same perks as DreamMore.
must_try: Ember & Elm restaurant and the nature-inspired rooms

name: Fly Fishing the Smokies
address: 1420 Fighting Creek Gap Rd, Gatlinburg, TN 37738
description: Award-winning, all-inclusive guide service teaching total beginners fly fishing in the pristine National Park streams.
must_try: Hazel Creek Guided Day Trip

name: The Smoky Mountain Angler
description: Oldest authorized fishing guide service in the National Park. Wade trips and float trips for all skill levels.
must_try: Smallmouth Bass Float Trip

name: Gatlinburg Golf Course
description: Only public golf course in the Gatlinburg area. 18 holes designed by William Langford, carved into the foothills with mountain views on every hole.
must_try: The signature par-3 12th hole with mountain backdrop

name: Alum Cave Trail to Mt. LeConte
address: Alum Cave Trailhead, Newfound Gap Rd
description: 10.9 miles round trip to the summit, 4.6 miles to Alum Cave Bluffs. Geological formations, wildflowers, and LeConte Lodge at the top (reservations required, supplies delivered by llama). One of the best day hikes in the Eastern US.
must_try: Hike to Alum Cave Bluffs at minimum, full LeConte if you're fit

name: Chimney Tops Trail
address: Chimney Tops Trailhead, Newfound Gap Rd
description: 3.2 miles round trip, strenuous. Rock scrambles and exposed ridgelines. Panoramic summit views. One of the most rewarding short hikes in the park.
must_try: The summit panorama

name: Laurel Falls Trail
address: Fighting Creek Gap Rd, Gatlinburg, TN
description: 2.6 miles round trip, paved, moderate. The most popular waterfall hike in the park. 80-foot falls. Gets crowded — go early or weekday.
must_try: The falls view at the end

name: Clingmans Dome
description: Highest point in the park (6,643 ft). Observation tower with 360-degree views on clear days. 0.5-mile steep paved walk from parking lot. AT crosses through.
must_try: Clear-day panoramic view from the tower

name: Cades Cove
address: Cades Cove Loop Rd, Townsend, TN
description: 11-mile one-way loop road through a historic valley. Black bears, white-tailed deer, wild turkeys, and historic cabins. Best at sunrise before the traffic hits. Wednesday/Saturday mornings bikes-only until 10AM.
must_try: Sunrise drive or the Wednesday bike-only morning
seasonal: Open year-round, loop road may close temporarily in winter

name: Great Smoky Mountains National Park
description: Most visited national park in the US — 12M+ annual visitors. 522,000 acres, 850+ miles of trails, 2,000+ species of plants, black bears, elk, synchronous fireflies. Free entry, $5/day parking pass required.
must_try: Cades Cove loop, Clingmans Dome, Laurel Falls, the synchronous firefly event (lottery in June)
seasonal: Newfound Gap Rd open year-round; Clingmans Dome Rd closed Dec-Mar

name: Ijams Nature Center
description: 315 acres of trails in South Knoxville. Mead's Quarry for kayaking, River Boardwalk with Tennessee River views, rock climbing. Free admission. Dogs on leash welcome.
must_try: River Boardwalk Trail and kayaking at Mead's Quarry

name: Roaring Fork Motor Nature Trail
address: Accessible from Historic Nature Trail, Gatlinburg
description: 5.5-mile one-way loop drive starting in Gatlinburg. Old-growth forest, historic buildings, and trailheads for Grotto Falls and Rainbow Falls. Less crowded than Cades Cove.
must_try: Grotto Falls trail (walk behind the waterfall)

name: Pink Jeep Tours Smoky Mountains
address: 131 The Island Dr #3105, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: Guided Jeep tours through the national park and surrounding areas. Multiple route options. Good for families and people who want the Smokies experience without the planning.
must_try: Custom Smoky Mountain Tour

name: Smoky Mountain Outdoors
description: Top-tier whitewater rafting on the Pigeon River. Guides are fantastic at making beginners feel completely safe.
must_try: Upper River Trip (Class III-IV rapids)

name: Smoky Mountain River Rat
description: The best outfitter for lazy afternoon tubing on the Little River or adrenaline-pumping whitewater rafting in Hartford.
must_try: Renting a riverside cabana after tubing

name: CLIMB Works Smoky Mountains
description: World-class zipline canopy tour surrounded by the National Park. Your feet won't touch the ground for over two hours.
must_try: The Mountaintop Zipline Tour

name: Legacy Mountain Ziplines
address: 2431 Upper Middle Creek Rd, Sevierville, TN 37876
description: Longest ziplines on the East Coast with staggering 360-degree Smokies views while flying up to 50 mph.
must_try: The 7-cable canopy tour

name: Enterprise Rent-A-Car - McGhee Tyson Airport
description: Directly at the Knoxville airport. Most reliable option for picking up an SUV or AWD vehicle to handle steep cabin roads.
must_try: Book an AWD vehicle for mountain driving

name: Shell - Last Gas Before the Park
description: The last reliable gas station before entering Great Smoky Mountains National Park. Do not skip this if driving to Clingmans Dome or Newfound Gap.
must_try: Fill up completely before hitting Newfound Gap Road

name: NOC Gatlinburg (Nantahala Outdoor Center)
description: 18,000-square-foot outdoor superstore at the park entrance. Trail maps, bear spray, rain jackets, and guided excursion bookings. Talk to the master guides.
must_try: Trail recommendations from the master guides

name: Food City - Gatlinburg
description: The go-to grocery store for stocking your Gatlinburg cabin. Carries firewood, fresh produce, local meats, and Smoky Mountain branded products.
must_try: Local Smoky Mountain branded products and firewood

name: Kroger - Pigeon Forge
address: 220 Wears Valley Rd, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: Massive supermarket at the Wears Valley / Pigeon Forge intersection. Perfect for bulk cabin provisioning runs. Online curbside pickup available.
must_try: Online curbside pickup to save time

name: Publix - Pigeon Forge
description: Immaculately clean grocery in Pigeon Forge. Grab high-quality deli meats, cheeses, and the famous Pub Subs for a trail picnic.
must_try: Publix sub sandwich for a trail lunch

name: Smoky Dog Lodge
description: Cage-free daycare and boarding facility. Drop your dog here while you hit Dollywood or the National Park. They treat animals like royalty.
must_try: The luxury cabana boarding suites

name: CVS Pharmacy - Pigeon Forge
description: Centrally located pharmacy on the Pigeon Forge strip. Essential for forgotten toiletries, first aid supplies, or allergy meds for mountain pollen.
must_try: Over-the-counter allergy meds for mountain pollen

name: Walgreens - Pigeon Forge
description: 24-hour store at a major Parkway intersection. Lifesaver for late-night essentials after attractions close.
must_try: Quick photo printing for vacation memories

name: Urgent Care of the Smokies
description: Walk-in clinic next to Publix. Fast, friendly, and saves you from an overwhelmed ER for minor vacation injuries and illnesses.
must_try: Online booking to hold your place in line

name: The Village Shops
description: European-style courtyard shopping. The Donut Friar, Pepper Palace, and a bunch of quirky shops. Been here since 1969.
must_try: The Donut Friar inside the village

name: Great Smoky Arts & Crafts Community
address: Glades Rd / Buckhorn Rd / Birds Creek Rd, Gatlinburg, TN
description: 8-mile loop road with 100+ independent artisans and craftspeople. Pottery, woodwork, leather, brooms, candles. Largest group of independent artisans in North America. The anti-Parkway experience.
must_try: Drive or trolley the loop and stop wherever catches your eye

name: Tanger Outlets Sevierville
description: 100+ outlet stores along the Parkway. Nike, Coach, Kate Spade, etc. Two separate locations (Sevierville 1 and 2). Good rainy-day plan.
must_try: Smith Creek Moonshine has a tasting bar inside

name: Mast General Store - Knoxville
description: Old-fashioned general store on Gay Street. Candy counter, outdoor gear, Appalachian goods. A Knoxville institution.
must_try: Old-fashioned candy by the pound

name: The Old Mill Square
address: 175 Old Mill Ave, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: Historic water-powered grist mill from 1830 surrounded by shops, pottery, candy kitchen, and restaurants. Old Mill grits and cornmeal are legendary. The General Store has everything.
must_try: Buy stone-ground cornmeal from the actual mill

name: LeConte Wellness Center
address: 170 Community Center Dr, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: Inside the Pigeon Forge Community Center. Affordable drop-in workout, group fitness classes, and indoor walking track.
must_try: Drop-in yoga or indoor walking track

name: Smoky Mountain Massage Therapy
description: Mobile massage therapists who bring the experience directly to your cabin deck. In-cabin couples massage is the signature move.
must_try: In-cabin Couples Massage

name: Foxplace Salon & Spa
description: Cozy boutique day spa in Gatlinburg known for incredible European steam facials and highly personalized therapeutic treatments.
must_try: European Steam Facial

name: St. Somewhere Spa at Margaritaville
address: 131 The Island Dr, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
description: Tropical-themed spa inside Margaritaville Island Hotel. High-end pedicures, massages, and a quiet chill room.
must_try: Volcano Hot Stone Massage

name: The Spa at Oak Haven Resort
description: Award-winning day spa tucked into a luxury cabin resort. The ultimate escape from Parkway neon and noise.
must_try: 80-minute Head to Toe Harmony experience

name: Wake Foot Sanctuary
description: Communal foot soaking sanctuary with wine/beer. Soak your feet in mineral baths while sipping cocktails. Strange concept, incredible execution. Market Square.
must_try: Signature foot soak with a glass of wine

name: Mountain Zen Yoga
description: Mobile yoga service bringing mats, music, and certified instructors directly to your cabin or preferred outdoor setting. Great for bachelorette groups.
must_try: Bachelorette group yoga session
